record.paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
record.original_question: What is the precise nature of the accretion–outflow connection in relativistic jet sources, to what extent is the outflow controlled by properties of the central compact object rather than only by the accretion flow, and what role does black-hole spin play in driving outflows in X-ray binaries and, by analogy, in active galactic nuclei?

evidence.quote: a strong accretion–outflow connection is indicated in all cosmic jet sources (including young stellar objects) but that its precise nature remains a puzzle. Relativistic jet sources could potentially provide new insights into this problem. For example, the extent to which the outflow is influenced by the properties of the central object (rather than by those of the accretion flow alone) is one important issue that could be explicitly addressed in this case. In particular, one could attempt to clarify the role of the black-hole spin in driving XRB outflows by comparing the properties of neutron-star and black-hole systems94 and then use the established analogies with AGNs to assess the applicability of the results to extragalactic jets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider compact accreting astrophysical systems that produce collimated relativistic outflows ("jets"), namely (i) Galactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) containing either a stellar-mass black hole or a neutron star accreting from a companion star, and (ii) active galactic nuclei (AGNs) powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole. In every such class of source, observations indicate a tight connection between the accretion flow (parametrized e.g. by the X-ray spectral state, mass accretion rate, and disc geometry) and the launching, power, and morphology of the outflow.

Provide a precise physical and quantitative characterization of this accretion–outflow connection. In particular, address the following:

1. Determine to what extent the properties of the outflow (its kinetic luminosity, bulk Lorentz factor, collimation, duty cycle, and on/off state transitions) are governed by intrinsic properties of the central compact object — its mass M, spin parameter a*, magnetic flux threading the horizon, and the presence or absence of a solid surface — as opposed to being determined solely by properties of the accretion flow (accretion rate, disc inner radius, magnetization, radiative state).

2. Quantify the role of black-hole spin a* ∈ [0,1) in driving relativistic jets from XRBs. Specifically, decide whether jet power scales with spin in accordance with a Blandford–Znajek-type prediction P_jet ∝ a*^2 (or a stronger monotonic dependence), and establish this by a controlled comparison between black-hole XRBs and neutron-star XRBs of comparable accretion rate.

3. Using the empirical fundamental-plane-type scaling relations between XRBs and AGNs (mass-invariant disc–jet coupling), determine whether and how the conclusions reached for stellar-mass black holes extrapolate to supermassive black holes powering extragalactic jets.

A complete solution would yield a predictive theory of jet launching, identifying the dominant physical mechanism (e.g. Blandford–Znajek, Blandford–Payne, magnetically arrested disc), the functional dependence of jet power on (M, a*, Ṁ, magnetic flux), and the observational signatures distinguishing spin-driven from disc-driven outflows across the full mass range of accreting compact objects.
artifact.status_search_result: The accretion–outflow connection and the precise role of black-hole spin in launching relativistic jets remain active research topics. Recent 2024–2025 work (e.g. Nature Astronomy studies tying the fastest jets to the BH spin axis, MNRAS 2025 disc–jet coupling analyses, and ongoing Cygnus X-1 observations) provides increasing empirical support for spin-powered jets via Blandford–Znajek-type mechanisms, but a definitive, quantitative theory linking jet power to (M, a*, Ṁ, magnetic flux) and unifying XRBs with AGNs has not been established.

status_evidence.title: The connection between the fastest astrophysical jets and the spin axis of their black hole
status_evidence.snippet: The most relativistic jets propagate along the spin axis of the black hole that launches them; the fastest jets are exclusively from black holes and locked to a fixed axis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent observational evidence (2025) supports a connection between BH spin axis and the fastest jets, but the underlying launching theory is still being developed.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting disc–jet coupling in black hole X-ray binaries
status_evidence.snippet: Examines disc dynamics and jet velocity coupling in BH XRBs (2025).
status_evidence.claim: Disc–jet coupling in XRBs remains an active area of investigation in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Jet production in black hole X-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses mass feeding and advection of magnetic fields as drivers of jet production across XRBs and AGNs.
status_evidence.claim: The relative role of accretion-flow properties versus central-object properties in jet launching is still under debate.
